$comment: ACKNOWLEDGED GAPS. An acknowledged gap is not an unknown.
UNKNOWN            we could not establish the state -> exit 2
ACKNOWLEDGED_GAP   we established it, it is bad, and someone owns it -> exit 0
The difference is that a gap has a name, an owner, a reason and a date.
Nothing may be listed here to make a red verifier green: the entry must
describe a real decision, and the verifier still PRINTS every gap on every
run so they cannot fade into the background.
Removing a gap is how it gets fixed. Adding one is a decision, not a repair.

gaps.reason: The sanctioned project-scoped path (mcp__supabase__*) is not connected — its OAuth flow has not been completed. Until it is, the account-scoped connector is the ONLY working Supabase query path, and it carries no read_only enforcement: a DELETE reaches production and nothing intercepts it. Denying it would remove the capability without making anything safe, and #1671 is the story of a document killing a working path. Retained deliberately as TEMPORARY_FALLBACK and named UNENFORCED rather than called safe.
gaps.closes_when: mcp__supabase__* is connected and exercised, after which this grant is removed.

gaps.reason: Measured 2026-08-29 with ten disposable probes: filesystem sandboxing is NOT enforced. Writes inside the project, writes outside it, writes to .claude/settings.json and .claude/hooks, reads of .env.local, and ../ traversal all SUCCEEDED — including paths the config lists under denyRead and denyWithinAllow. sandbox.filesystem.disabled is true and authoritative. Network sandboxing IS enforced (observed: deny network-outbound analytics.brew.sh:443). Enabling it was NOT done: the configured allowWrite list covers only /private/tmp/helmv3-*, /tmp/helmv3-*, ~/.npm and ~/Library/Caches/deno — not the repository — so flipping it as configured would block every worktree write, and the setting is user-global so it would do that to every project and any concurrent session. Consequence accepted: Bash writes into the canonical checkout remain structurally unblocked; guard-canonical-write.mjs covers only Write/Edit/MultiEdit.
gaps.closes_when: an allowWrite set is designed that permits worktrees and denies canonical, and its behaviour is proven on a disposable profile before being applied user-globally.

gaps.reason: The owner authorization for applying production migrations through the project-scoped MCP is explicit and repeated. But that server's OAuth grant requests ONLY :read scopes — organizations, projects, database, analytics, secrets, edge_functions, environment, storage. A token minted under those scopes structurally cannot write, so the authorized capability probably cannot function as granted. This is surfaced rather than resolved: confirming it means attempting a production migration, which this run is not authorized to do and should not do to answer a documentation question.
gaps.closes_when: the owner either completes the OAuth flow and observes what apply_migration actually does, or moves migrations to a path whose capability matches the authorization.

gaps.reason: Measured 2026-08-30: admin_events reported 0 error-or-worse rows in 48h while Sentry reported 12 unresolved issues, several receiving events within hours. Both were correct, and the cause is now precise — TWO causes, not one. (1) CLASSIFICATION: Sentry's largest issue ([v3.llm.budget.platform_default], 64 events) IS in admin_events, 25 rows, at severity INFO, because an unconfigured coach budget falling back to the platform default is expected. Sentry has no severity model. (2) SCOPE: JWT expired, heartbeat 401s, fetch failed, invalid credentials and the coerce error have ZERO admin_events rows — they are unhandled framework/platform errors that never reached logServerError, which src/instrumentation.ts documents as intended. NO CAPTURE PATH VIOLATES THE CONTRACT. The defect is what Mission Control CLAIMS: one surface's zero standing in for production health. Contract written to docs/OBSERVABILITY_AUTHORITY.md.
gaps.closes_when: The board renders the two surfaces separately and marks overall health as partial when they are unreconciled — per the model in docs/OBSERVABILITY_AUTHORITY.md. Explicitly NOT closed by making every Sentry event appear in admin_events: that would discard the severity grading that makes admin_events useful.

gaps.reason: The #1681 fix requires positive owner intent before parking a checkout whose branch has an OPEN PR. It does NOT cover a worktree whose branch has no PR at all — there, reproducibility alone still decides, exactly as before. That is the same defect class: a session working in a worktree BEFORE opening a PR is clean, pushed and invisible to lsof between tool calls, and has no row in config/open-pr-dispositions.json because there is no PR to key one on. Left open rather than closed by extending the rule, because requiring recorded intent for every branch would make --park unable to act at all, and parking exists so an open PR waiting on a human stops costing ~3.8 GiB. Narrower in practice than it reads: HELM_MAX_MUTATION_WORKTREES defaults to 1, so a second concurrent mutation workspace is refused before it can be created.
gaps.closes_when: a worktree carries a durable ownership marker independent of its PR — a session id written at creation by scripts/new-worktree.sh and checked for liveness — or the mutation budget is proven to make concurrent PR-less worktrees unreachable.

closed.how: Measured what the gh path actually exposes: authenticated account id (238133540), repository id (1119265234) and the OAuth scope set from the X-Oauth-Scopes response header (gist, read:org, repo, workflow). All stable, none of it secret material. That is a capability fingerprint, so drift IS detectable — the gap was closed by measuring rather than by changing any lifecycle code, which is what its closing condition asked for.

computeTeamGrade gained an explicit UNKNOWN grade, checked BEFORE every other rule so a dormant team with an unreadable count is ungradeable rather than graded D by luck. team-page-extras resolves a rejected read to null instead of 0, the page renders an em-dash with an explaining title and adds errors7d to its existing degraded banner, and computeTeamComputedInsights no longer prints "fully active with no errors" from an unread count. Regression tests cover the grade, the insights strip and the producer — the producer one exists because reverting it to 0 TYPECHECKS CLEANLY (number is assignable to number|null), so only a behavioural test stops it coming back.
